note: Drafted on 2026-11-15 by an AI session under D34 of issue #77, for rotation B. D197 of issue #77 (inputs computed as AMG computes them, so the model is used as it was calibrated). The id, scope key crop and unit are those engine/residues/_parameters.py reads on main (RECORDS, CROP_SCOPE_KEY); the scope value is the crop_id of demonstration rotation B (D128). Row: the spring wheat row, as D142 and D197 of issue #77 take it; the row "MC, Winter wheat" prints the same h_AG, h_BG, C_conc_AG and C_conc_BG. Verbatim row to compare, parameters_PLANT.tab: "MC,Spring wheat,Blé de printemps,C3,0.425,0.409,0.101,0.066,0.96,0.51,7.517,0.5,0.217,0.4,0.44,0.4,Solebiom project" (header "Crop_type,Crop_name,Crop_name_FR,Plant_group,RP,RS,RR,RE,Beta,HI,SR,PSS,h_AG,h_BG,C_conc_AG,C_conc_BG,Source"); C_conc_BG = 0.4. Definition, AMGv2_parameter_list.tab: "C content of the belowground crop residues", unit "gC.g-1 DW": a ratio of masses, written dimensionless as EP4 requires (C1.1). Second check: Clivot et al. (2019), printed p. 102: "assuming a C content of 0.40 g g-1 in the BG plant material (Boiffin et al., 1986)". The dataset description says: "They are applicable for average French arable crop conditions." D192 and D197 of issue #77 take them as French defaults, not calibrated for Uruguay, and say so in the label. Per D161 no AI session writes a person's name in checked_by: the lead developer, or their delegate (D66), fills it after comparing the text with the source.
